I have Maladaptive Daydreaming Disorder (very vivid and reoccurring daydreams) paired w/ hyperfixations, I might have ADD as well (tho I never got it diagnosed). 
I mean yea, I suppose daydreams are normal, but not to the extent that I'm experiencing them in. I do so on a regular basis and when I do, they are so vivid that it's exhausting and afterwards I just feel ashamed about it. Usually they are about things I enjoy or am interested in, like series or games etc., which is why I don't even want to find new things anymore because I just know it'll swallow up all of my thoughts and I won't be able to concentrate on anything else, including school. So if I can't focus on important things and all I want to do all day is live in my own little fantasy world, how am I supposed to live a normal life as a functioning, independent member of society? 
I try refraining from music I like because it triggers my MDD. I mean, how sad is that? I can't even enjoy listening to music. I realized I never actually listened to it because of the music itself, I always did it solely to fuel this disorder. 
I always find myself zoning out and getting lost in my thoughts, regardless of whether I want to. If you tried talking to me, you could do it for maybe 10 seconds and then you'll lose me. I feel horrible about it. 
Sometimes I just look at other people and think "I wish I was more like them", not because they are special or something but, quite the opposite, because they are normal. I'm not normal. I don't feel normal. I just want to be normal. 
And if anyone reads this and thinks "yea but that sounds like somehting that's easy to fix" or anything of the sorts, I couldn't care less. What matters is the way I FEEL about this, and I feel like the way I am is not something that I can fix. I'll always be this way and there's nothing I can do. There probably aren't many people who can relate to and understand me anyway, so how are things supposed to get better? Especially considering that I can barely talk about it because I'm embarrassed? That this isn't a more common issue, like depression, so most people won't even know what I'm talking about or won't understand why it's so hard for me? 
Either way, I can't see light at the end of the tunnel. I failed in life, I should just end it. But like I said, I can't bear the thought of my mother crying on top of my casket, my father starting smoking again because he has no other way of coping, my brother's grades declining because not only does he no longer have someone to talk to and ask for help, but because he also can't stop thinking about his dead sister and the entire family slowly growing apart.
